intended_object: For an extension of number fields L/K and an infinite place w of K, this is the map of Aut(L/K)-modules I_L → (K_w ⊗_K L)ˣ ≅ ∏_{w'|w} L_{w'}ˣ that sends an idele to its components at the places of L above w. The docstring and the module documentation say so.
explanation:
The definition is a composite of three maps:
1. It projects the ideles to the infinite ideles (L ⊗ ℝ)ˣ.
2. It applies the library's isomorphism `infiniteIdelesPiIso`, which identifies the infinite ideles with the product over the infinite places w of K of (K_w ⊗_K L)ˣ.
3. It takes the w-th factor with `Rep.piProj`.

The simp lemma `coe_idelesToInfiniteSemilocalUnits_hom_apply` confirms what the map does: its underlying value is `infiniteAdeleSemilocalHom L w` applied to the infinite-adele part of the idele. So it is the standard semi-local component at an archimedean place, and it is a morphism of Galois representations, as the docstring says.

The setting needs no further generality. Infinite places are what make this a number-field notion, and the map is a specific object in that setting. Mathlib has no semi-local unit or idele-component maps of this kind as morphisms of `Rep`, so there is no Mathlib counterpart.
